newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks fade at open after Dow dims.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks fade at open after Dow dims.

text.p: The Australian share market was marked down modestly at the open on Tuesday as investors factored in the effects of a weaker Dow Jones industrial average and the continued decline of base metal prices on the London Metal Exchange.
At 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 5.7 points lower at 2,334.1.
The December share price index was six points down at 2,356 and at a 21.9 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said the early fall was a knee-jerk reaction to offshore moves and investor sentiment was still positive.
"I think this market is still quite bullish and I wouldn't be surprised if it tested life-time high levels later today," a dealer from a Brisbane-based brokerage said.
The dealer said the U.S. market was expected to remain firm in the lead up to the presidential election and this factor was underpinning the positive tone of the Australian market.
"The most negative point for the market is base metal prices. Copper and aluminium have been very weak lately and this is hurting the big miners," the dealer said.
The return of Sydney investors after a public holiday in New South Wales on Monday lifted volume to usual levels.
At 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), life office National Mutual listed at A$1.75 per share, a 15-cent or 9.4-percent premium to its institutional share offer price of A$1.60.
